title: Finite type algebras over arbitrary domains are generically flat
statement: Let R and B be commutative rings with R an integral domain, and let φ : R → B be a finite type ring map [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. There is a nonzero a ∈ R such that, for every B-algebra T that is a localization of B at φ(a) [def-weil-ring-localization-away], the composite R → B → T is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No Noetherian, finite presentation, or injectivity hypothesis on φ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 051T, finite type algebra case with M = B; Tag 051S, finite-presentation descent to a Noetherian subring; Tag 051R, Noetherian generic freeness

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation P → B over R and let K be the fraction field of R. The relation ideal in K[t_1,...,t_n] is finitely generated by the Hilbert basis theorem. Lift finitely many generators, clearing denominators, to the kernel over R and form their finitely presented quotient B_prime. The map B_prime → B is surjective and an isomorphism over K.

Following Tag 051S, descend the finite presentation of B_prime to the subring R_0 generated over the integers by its finitely many coefficients. R_0 is a Noetherian domain. Noetherian generic freeness makes the descended algebra free over (R_0)_a for a nonzero a. Base change gives a free R_a-module B_prime_a; the image of a in R is still nonzero.

The kernel of B_prime_a → B_a vanishes after extension to K. Since a free module over the domain R_a injects into its scalar extension to K, that kernel is zero already. Thus B_a is free over R_a, hence flat over R_a and over R. The universal property of localization transports this flatness to every localization model T. The zero algebra is included: take a = 1.

theorem exists_nonzero_flat_localizationAway {R B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [IsDomain R] (φ : R →+* B) (hφ : φ.FiniteType) :
    ∃ a : R, a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ (T : Type u) [CommRing T] [Algebra B T]
      [IsLocalization.Away (φ a) T], ((algebraMap B T).comp φ).Flat
